newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris stocks get some respite from firmer Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Paris stocks get some respite from firmer Wall St.

text.p: French shares ventured into positive territory after Wall Street stocks opened broadly higher but slipped back to show a small loss.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index, which had struggled to break through 2,020 under its own steam before the New York opening, rose to 2,021.27, up 0.85 points, on the Dow's firmer opening before subsiding to around 2,020.13, down 0.29 points.
The broader SBF 120 index was off 0.11 points at 1,422.98.
The Dow was showing a gain of 0.13 percent at the same time.
Before Wall Street opened, the CAC-40 had spent most of the morning down around four points or 0.2 percent.
* Supermarkets group Carrefour gained after brokerage and research firm Cheuvreux de Virieu confirmed the stock on its buy list, a fund manager said.
* Reinsurance group Scor up on news that British insurer Prudential had sold its Mercantile & General reinsurance business to Swiss Re.

* Bollore nearly two percent lower after suspension during which it said it had approved plans to buy out its 73.83 percent owned transport unit Scac Delmas Vileujeux (SDV) and invited shareholders to tender their shares.
* UIC retraces a third of its 11.55 franc opening loss triggered by first-half data released on Monday evening.
